title: Laser treatment for varicose veins (EVLT)
what: The doctor puts a thin laser fiber into the damaged vein and seals it from the inside with a laser. Blood then flows through healthy veins. There are no cuts, only a needle puncture.
why: For varicose veins, when the damaged vein disrupts blood flow: heavy legs, swelling, and enlarged veins on the legs.
duration: the procedure usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; you go home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to do
If you ever had blood clots in your veins

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: A leg vein ultrasound and blood tests are required before the procedure. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Compression
prepare.text: You usually buy a compression stocking in your size beforehand. The doctor will tell you the class and size.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast. The procedure is done under local numbing. A light breakfast is fine. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not put cream on your leg on the day of the procedure. Ask your clinic whether to shave your leg.

bring: Your vein ultrasound and test results
steps: Using ultrasound, the doctor marks the damaged vein on your skin
The leg is cleaned, and the vein is punctured under local numbing
A thin laser fiber is put into the vein
A numbing solution is injected under the skin along the vein. This is several small shots
The laser is turned on and the fiber is slowly pulled out. The vein is sealed
A compression stocking is put on your leg
feel: The numbing shots are unpleasant, but bearable
During the laser: warmth or light tingling
If it hurts, tell the doctor
after: Right after the procedure, you need to walk for 30 to 60 minutes
The stocking is usually worn for 1 to 4 weeks, as your doctor plans
Bruising and a pulling pain along the vein usually last 1 to 2 weeks
For 2 to 3 weeks: no bathhouse, sauna, hot bath, or heavy sports
A check-up ultrasound in a few days or weeks, as your doctor says
red_flags: Your leg swells a lot, your calf hurts, or the leg turns hot or bluish
Sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing up blood: call emergency services right away
A fever over 38 degrees, or redness and pus at the puncture site

faq.a: With local numbing, it is usually bearable. The most unpleasant part is the numbing shots along the vein.

faq.q: How long do I wear the stocking after EVLT?
faq.a: Usually 1 to 4 weeks. The plan is made for each person. In the first days, you take it off almost never.
A sealed vein does not reopen, but other veins may widen over time. That is why you need check-ups with your doctor.

reminders.text: Laser vein treatment tomorrow. Bring your compression stocking, ultrasound and test results, and loose trousers.
